summary: First iteration full-stack test of Norwegian date invitation app. Backend (8 pytest tests) and frontend (mobile + desktop UI flows) all PASS. All 3 buttons (A/B/C) correctly transition to localized success state and reset works. Telegram intentionally unconfigured -> telegram_sent=false with clear error (expected, not a bug).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py uses deprecated @app.on_event('shutdown'); consider FastAPI lifespan handler (non-blocking, minor).
TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is empty in /app/backend/.env by design — user must populate it before going to production. Health endpoint correctly exposes telegram_configured=false for visibility.
Frontend hero image URL is hardcoded in Invitation.jsx — acceptable for SPA, but could be moved to a constants file for easier swap.

No rate limiting on POST /api/respond — a public-facing endpoint that writes to Mongo and (when configured) hits Telegram is abuse-prone. Consider basic rate limiting or honeypot before sharing the URL publicly.
seed_data_creation: Test posts inserted into Mongo collection 'invitation_responses' with TEST_ prefixed notes for traceability. No cleanup performed (small volume).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py and cover health, all 3 choices (A/B/C), invalid choice (422), optional note, missing field validation, and Mongo persistence. Frontend tested at 390x844 (mobile) and 1920x1080 (desktop). All data-testids verified: invitation-root, invitation-heading, invitation-subheading, btn-accept, btn-maybe, btn-decline, success-message, btn-reset, error-message. When TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN gets populated, re-run backend tests — the assertion that telegram_sent==False must be relaxed (currently expects empty token).
